newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 15.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Tuesday:
* The market's focus will still be on currency-sensitive issues as investors await the peso to stabilise, Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook.

* Volatility will continue to characterise the market. Investors are advised to be selective and strong dips should be considered as good buying opportunities, said BPI Securities Corp analyst Roberto Cano.
* On Monday, the Philippine composite index ended 9.59 points up at 2,710.73.
* The Dow Jones on Monday ended 1.16 points higher at 7,922.98. PLDT's ADR closed up $0 7/8 at $33 1/2.
* The Philippine peso ended at $26 to a dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 32.375 percent vs 32.15625 percent.

* The peso slumped on Monday after its de facto devaluation but an initial surge in the share market quickly fizzled out. The Central Bank launched a witch-hunt to find out if any local banks were involved in last week's repeated speculative attacks on the peso which resulted in the currency's 11.5 percent plunge to near four-year lows.
* Philipine President Fidel Ramos said the present level of the peso was reasonable.
* The peso settled at 30.50 to the U.S. dollar in the unofficial parallel market in Manila, weaker than the 29 peso close in the official market, traders said on Monday.

* The Philippines is likely to attain a trade balance earlier than its target of year 2001 due to the sharp depreciation of its local currency against the U.S. dollar, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said.
* The Philippines' gross international reserves had gone down to $9.7 billion as of Monday morning, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Gabriel Singson said.
* The Philippine 91-day treasury bill yield rose to 13.214 percent from the previous 12.175 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said.
* The Central Bank is looking at the foreign currency positions of banks to make sure they stay within prudent levels, Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said.
